plain_text:
1 
 
DRAFT Meeting Minutes 
 
 
Salem Bicycling & Shared Path Advisory Committee 
 
Wednesday, November 4, 2026 | 6:15 p.m. 
 
City Hall Annex 1st Floor Meeting Room & Via Remote Participation 
 
Members Present: John Wathne (Chair), Josiah Guthrie (Vice Chair), Catrina Meyer, 
Alexa Ogno, Craig Bilodeau, Matt Caruso, Kevin Jordan, Josh 
Nagle 
Members Absent:  Annie Wolf 
Also Present:  Tom Devine, Senior Planner 
 
Call Meeting to Order 
 
Wathne calls the meeting to order. 
 
Welcome New Member 
 
Committee members welcome and introduce themselves to newly appointed member 
Catrina Meyer. 
 
Public Comment 
 
Wathne opens public comment and there is none. 
 
Discussion of Bike Master Plan and Role of the Committee 
 
Devine proposes that the intern, who is researching ways various bike advocacy groups 
achieve a meaningful impact, present his findings at the December meeting. The 
Committee is interested in hosting this presentation. Caruso asks about follow up on the 
option to create a nonprofit group. Ogno describes what she presented at the prior 
meeting. Meyer notes that there is a national street safety group that does local 
chapters. 
 
Discussion of Potential Neighborways in Salem 
 
Jordan describes the neighborways concept and notes that it can include contraflow 
bike lanes on one-way streetds. Guthrie mentions a website with design information for 
neighborways. Meyer adds that these are also called Bicycle Boulevards. The group 
contemplates having a unifying theme for neighborways, such as following historic 
trolley routes. Ogno notes the characteristics of Somerville’s neighborways, including 
bump outs and one-way pinch points on two-way streets.
2 
 
The group wishes to schedule a Bike Committee tour of Somerville neighborways. They 
will meet on Saturday, December 5 at the Salem train station. Devine will post the event 
as required. 
 
Bikeshare Program Updates 
 
Devine reports that he has completed outreach to neighboring communities to share 
information to support consideration of expanding the system into their municipalities. 
Nagle asks for October ridership data and Devine commits to providing it by email. 
 
Events 
 
Devine remarks that the MassBike/MassCEC e-bike workshop that the Committee is 
cohosting is scheduled for 4-6pm tomorrow (November 5). The City’s Sustainability 
Engagement Coordinator, Stacy Kilb, has let the Committee know about the November 
9 Salem Resource & Energy Fair. 
 
Devine asks if the Bike Committee would like to host a Safe Routes to School e-bike 
safety forum. Meyer recalls one of these events involving schools and police in a 
community conversation and suggests there should be more focus on guidance for 
parents about which bikes are appropriate for children. Ogno suggests hosting this 
event early next year before the spring season. 
 
Transportation Commission Update 
 
Ogno reports that there was no meeting in October. 
 
Staff Update 
 
Devine gives the group a heads up that a portion of the Salvo bike path will be closed 
for utility work during part of December. Devine believes the work is only to replace 
utility poles with no excavation in the bike path. The closure will be on the segment 
between Ocean Ave. and the Canal Street crossing. 
 
Ogno asks for the status of the regional rail trail feasibility study. Devine reports that he, 
along with staff from Peabody and Danvers, have reviewed consultant proposals for the 
work and are scheduled to interview shortlisted firms on Thursday. He hopes to execute 
a contract before the end of the calendar year for this project that will take up to two 
years to complete. 
 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Devine catches a typo. 
 
Bilodeau motions, Nagle seconds, and all vote in favor to approve the October 7 
minutes with an edit.
3 
 
 
Adjourn 
 
Caruso motions, Jordan seconds, and all vote in favor to adjourn at 7:15pm.
